name: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework (IMDA MGF) — Second Edition
description: Singapore IMDA/PDPC Model AI Governance Framework (Second Edition, 2020) overlay. Voluntary, principle-based framework for private sector organizations deploying AI in Singapore. Four governance areas: (1) Internal Governance Structures, (2) Human Involvement in Decision-Making, (3) Operations Management, (4) Stakeholder Communication. Strong companion signal with MAS TRM (mandatory for Singapore financial institutions). PDPC linkage makes personal data protection obligations directly regulatory.

evidence_requirements: Documented AI governance policy approved by senior management or board
AI governance committee or cross-functional AI governance structure evidenced by meeting records or organizational charter
AI deployment decision framework covering risk assessment, approval criteria, and lifecycle stages
Policy communicated to relevant personnel — awareness training records or acknowledgements
GOV-01.framework_reference: MGF Area 1 — Internal Governance Structures and Measures §2.1

evidence_requirements: Named individual or team accountable for each deployed AI system
Responsibility assignment documented in RACI matrix or equivalent governance artifact
Competence requirements for AI oversight roles defined and met
Accountability chain accessible internally and, where required, to affected stakeholders
GOV-02.framework_reference: MGF Area 1 — Internal Governance Structures and Measures §2.2

evidence_requirements: AI-specific risk assessment process documented — includes bias, accuracy degradation, misuse, and third-party risk dimensions
Risk acceptance thresholds defined and approved by senior management
Risk assessment conducted before AI system deployment and at material changes
Risk register maintained with treatment decisions and residual risk tracking
GOV-03.framework_reference: MGF Area 1 — Internal Governance Structures and Measures §2.3

evidence_requirements: Human oversight classification documented for each AI system: human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, or fully automated — with rationale
Higher-risk AI decisions mapped to increased human oversight requirements
Oversight configuration reviewed on material changes to AI system or deployment context
Explainability mechanisms in place appropriate to decision impact level
Documentation of rationale for oversight level selection, including risk basis
GOV-04.framework_reference: MGF Area 2 — Human Involvement in AI-Augmented Decision-Making §3.1–3.3

evidence_requirements: Inventory of AI systems in scope of governance program — minimum: system name, intended purpose, deployment context, accountable owner
Lifecycle stage tracked for each system (development, pilot, production, retired)

Note: MGF does not explicitly require a formal registry; coverage is inferred from governance accountability requirements — an org cannot demonstrate Area 1 compliance without knowing what is deployed
ID-01.framework_reference: MGF Area 1 — Internal Governance Structures and Measures (implied)

evidence_requirements: Third-party AI tools and components included in vendor risk assessment
AI-relevant terms addressed in vendor agreements — data handling, model change notification, incident reporting
Note: MGF Area 3 vendor management principles apply; no specific tool registry requirement stated
Data quality assessment documented for AI training and inference inputs — representativeness, bias screening, known limitations
Data governance procedures covering acquisition, labelling, validation, and disposal
Personal data handling in AI context documented with PDPC compliance linkage
Data sources and provenance documented for each AI system
Third-party AI components (models, APIs, datasets) assessed for risk before adoption
Supply chain risk assessment documents provenance, licensing, update cadence, and exit/replacement plan
Vendor dependency risk reviewed periodically and on material vendor changes
ID-04.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management §4.3 (third-party AI component risk)

evidence_requirements: AI system risk profile documented — severity of potential harm, breadth of impact, reversibility, and automation level
Risk profile determines oversight configuration (linkage to GOV-04 oversight classification)
Risk profile updated on material changes to system capability or deployment context
ID-05.framework_reference: MGF Areas 1+2 — risk assessment drives oversight level selection

evidence_requirements: Access controls for AI systems documented — who can modify, retrain, or access model outputs
Note: MGF Area 3 implies access controls in operations management but does not specify authentication standards; PDPC linkage applies for personal data access
PR-01.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management (access controls implied)

evidence_requirements: AI system permissions scoped to intended purpose — documented principle of data minimization in deployment
Note: MGF principle of limiting AI use to declared purpose aligns with scope enforcement; no specific technical control mandated
PR-02.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management (minimal access principle)

evidence_requirements: AI component integrity verified before deployment — third-party models and APIs assessed for authenticity
Change management process requires re-assessment on AI component updates
Note: MGF Area 3 vendor management and operations integrity principles apply; no explicit provenance verification standard cited
PR-03.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management §4.3 (AI system integrity)

evidence_requirements: Personal data exposure in AI outputs controlled and documented — PDPC Advisory on AI linkage applies
Data minimization applied to AI training data and inference outputs involving personal data
Consent and purpose limitation documented for personal data used in AI contexts
Cross-border data transfer controls applied where relevant to AI training/inference data
PR-04.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management §4.1 (data protection); PDPC Advisory on Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation Systems

evidence_requirements: Audit logs maintained for AI system actions — sufficient for accountability and contested decision review
Log records retained to support post-incident investigation and stakeholder accountability queries
Audit trail design documented — what is logged, retention period, access controls on logs
Logs accessible to internal accountability chain and, where required, to affected parties under Area 4
PR-05.framework_reference: MGF Areas 1+4 — accountability and stakeholder interaction

evidence_requirements: AI system configuration controls documented — change management process for model updates and parameter changes
Configuration baseline maintained with change approval process
Note: MGF Area 3 operations management implies configuration integrity; no specific configuration management standard cited
PR-06.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management (AI system integrity monitoring)

evidence_requirements: Data in transit protected for AI system communications — encryption applied to model API calls involving personal or sensitive data
Note: MGF Area 3 implies data security in operations; MAS TRM companion overlay provides specific encryption requirements for Singapore financial institutions
PR-07.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management (data security, implied)

evidence_requirements: AI system tested for robustness against adversarial inputs before deployment
AI Verify toolkit testing dimensions considered for robustness and safety validation
Input validation documented for AI system interfaces exposed to external or untrusted parties
Note: Project Moonshot (IMDA LLM eval toolkit) provides more explicit adversarial testing guidance as companion resource
PR-08.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management §4.2 (AI system testing); AI Verify Toolkit (companion resource)

evidence_requirements: Model performance monitoring implemented — tracks accuracy, drift, bias indicators, and output quality degradation
Monitoring thresholds defined with escalation triggers for significant drift
Monitoring results reviewed at defined intervals and on material events
Evidence of monitoring activity maintained — logs or dashboards showing ongoing surveillance
Configuration change detection in place for AI systems — alerts on unauthorized or unexpected changes
Note: MGF Area 3 implies configuration monitoring as part of operations management; no specific drift detection standard
DE-02.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management (change detection implied)

evidence_requirements: Internal governance audit process covers AI system compliance with policies and framework commitments
Compliance deviations tracked and remediated — audit records maintained
Note: MGF Area 1 continuous improvement and internal governance review principles apply
DE-03.framework_reference: MGF Area 1 — Internal Governance (governance audit and continuous improvement)

evidence_requirements: Audit log integrity maintained — controls to detect tampering with AI audit records
Evidence preservation for accountability purposes — records sufficient for contested decision review
Note: MGF Area 1 accountability requirements and Area 4 stakeholder appeal rights imply audit integrity obligations
DE-04.framework_reference: MGF Areas 1+4 — accountability and audit integrity

evidence_requirements: Incident response process documented for AI system failures, harmful outputs, and misuse events
Response playbook covers model rollback, output suppression, and stakeholder notification
Note: MGF Area 3 requires incident response process but does not mandate automated response — human decision remains appropriate for significant AI incidents
Human escalation pathway documented for high-risk AI decisions and contested AI outputs
Appeal or contestation mechanism available to individuals affected by consequential AI decisions
Escalation response SLA defined — timeline for human review of contested decisions
Escalation pathway tested periodically — evidence of test or drill records
RS-02.framework_reference: MGF Area 2 §3.2 (human review) and Area 4 §5.2 (contestation mechanism)

evidence_requirements: Incident evidence preserved sufficient for accountability review and post-incident analysis
Incident records maintained — timeline, affected systems, affected parties, response actions taken
Evidence package available for governance review or regulatory inquiry
RS-03.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management §4.4 (incident management and evidence)

evidence_requirements: AI model rollback capability demonstrated — ability to revert to prior model version on safety or quality failure
Rollback procedure documented and tested — evidence of test or drill
Recovery time objective defined for AI system restoration following incident
RC-01.framework_reference: MGF Area 3 — Operations Management §4.4 (model rollback and recovery)

evidence_requirements: Post-incident review process for AI events — root cause analysis, contributing factors, remediation plan
Lessons learned documented and fed back into AI governance program (Area 1 continuous improvement loop)
Governance committee notified of material AI incidents — evidence of board or senior management reporting
RC-02.framework_reference: MGF Areas 1+3 — continuous improvement and post-incident learning

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: Voluntary self-assessment. No mandatory certification or third-party audit required by MGF itself. Organizations may voluntarily use AI Verify (IMDA's AI testing toolkit) for self-assessment against MGF dimensions. MAS TRM companion overlay applies separate mandatory reporting for Singapore financial institutions.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: No mandatory external reporting under MGF. Internal governance reporting to board or senior management required (Area 1). PDPC notification obligations apply for personal data breaches involving AI systems under Singapore PDPA.
reporting_obligations.notes: MGF is a voluntary framework — no enforcement body and no penalty regime. Practical enforcement driver is MAS TRM (for financial institutions) and procurement requirements from Singapore government agencies. IMDA AI Verify toolkit (9 testing dimensions) provides structured self-assessment mechanism aligned to MGF.

human_oversight_mandates.description: MGF Area 2 explicitly requires organizations to determine the appropriate level of human involvement in AI-augmented decisions. For high-risk or consequential decisions, human-in-the-loop or human-on-the-loop oversight is required. Fully automated AI decisions affecting individuals must be documented with rationale and must include a contestation mechanism (Area 4). This makes human oversight configuration a core compliance element, not optional.
human_oversight_mandates.applies_to: Consequential AI decisions — those affecting individuals' rights, safety, financial interests, or significant life decisions

notes: Singapore IMDA Model AI Governance Framework Second Edition (2020). Published by IMDA and PDPC jointly. Voluntary, principle-based framework — the primary AI governance reference for Singapore private sector. Four governance areas map well to AKSI's three-tier architecture: Area 1 (Internal Governance) → GOV/ID controls; Area 2 (Human Oversight) → GOV-04/RS-02; Area 3 (Operations) → PR/DE/RS/RC controls; Area 4 (Stakeholder Communication) → PR-05/RS-02. The MGF's voluntary character means evidence is governance documentation rather than regulatory compliance artifacts. Practical compliance pressure comes from MAS TRM (mandatory for regulated financial institutions) and Singapore government procurement expectations. This overlay applies Singapore-specific governance evidence and mapping adjustments on top of the AKSI v0.6 common-control catalog. Because the framework is principle-based, many mappings remain partial rather than inapplicable. First Singapore MGF overlay — v0.2 planned to add AI Verify dimension-to-control mappings once available.
